consequence.statement: Any endpoint.tls.caOptional configuration present in ConsulCatalog or Nomad provider static configuration will be ignored in v3.
consequence.remediation: Remove the endpoint.tls.caOptional option from the ConsulCatalog and Nomad provider static configuration sections.

original.statement: The ConsulCatalog provider endpoint.tls.caOptional option and the Nomad provider endpoint.tls.caOptional option have been removed in v3.

consequence.statement: An endpoint.tls.caOptional value set in the ConsulCatalog or Nomad provider static configuration (file or CLI) is no longer honoured in v3 because the option has been removed.
consequence.remediation: Remove the endpoint.tls.caOptional option from the ConsulCatalog and Nomad provider static configuration.

corrected.statement: The endpoint.tls.caOptional option of the ConsulCatalog and Nomad providers has been removed in v3; a value configured there is no longer honoured, as TLS client authentication is a server-side option.

decision.reason: [ev-7482c113b845] and [ev-6c38c9ee7078] say the `endpoint.tls.CAOptional` option for both the ConsulCatalog and Nomad providers "has been removed in v3" and should be removed from static configuration. So a configured value stops being honoured, and setting-ignored (mandatory work) is the right kind. The evidence does not say whether a leftover key is silently ignored or rejected at startup. I therefore restated the consequence in the evidence's own terms rather than "will be ignored", and lowered severity from high to medium because the evidence gives nothing that supports high.
